title: CORS policy per route
description:
Browser front ends on other origins cannot call the gateway's routes today: their preflights reach the upstreams, which do not know about CORS, and the answers carry no allow headers. This adds a CORS policy to each route, answered by the gateway itself.

- Routes file `cors: {allow_origins, allow_methods, allow_headers, expose_headers, allow_credentials, max_age}`. `allow_origins` lists exact origins or `"*"` alone; `max_age` is a duration, at most 24h.
- A preflight (`OPTIONS` with `Origin` and `Access-Control-Request-Method`) is matched by the method it asks for and answered `204` by the gateway, before authentication, the rate limit and the upstream. Its allow fields are sent only to an allowed origin.
- Actual responses from an allowed origin get `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` and `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`, replacing any the upstream sent. `*` is sent only without credentials; with credentials the request's origin is echoed back. Disallowed origins get no CORS fields.
- Gateway errors (401, 429 and the rest) carry the same fields, so the browser can show them.
- Validation names the route and field. README documents the policy.

Tests: preflights with and without credentials, a disallowed origin, actual responses that replace the upstream's fields, the wildcard rules, gateway errors, and the validation messages.

bugs.summary: setCORS chooses Access-Control-Allow-Origin from the request's origin (it echoes the origin when the route lists specific origins or allows credentials, and leaves the field out for a disallowed origin or a request without one), but no response names Origin in Vary, and the preflight's Vary lists only the request-method and request-headers fields. The response therefore depends on a request header it does not declare: a shared cache in front of the gateway can store one origin's answer, or the answer to a request without an origin, and serve it to another origin's page, which the browser then refuses. Every response of a route with a CORS policy needs Origin in Vary, next to the upstream's own Vary fields, which copyResponseHeader copies before the CORS fields are set.
bugs.trigger: Route with allow_origins [https://app.example.com]: a request from that origin gets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com and no Origin in Vary; the answers to a disallowed origin and to a request without Origin have no Origin in Vary either; a preflight's Vary lists only the request-method and request-headers fields.
bugs.false_rebuttal: No Vary is needed: the origins a route accepts are a fixed list in the routes file, so each one gets the same answer every time and a cache keyed by URL cannot mix them up. CORSPolicy.Allow in internal/core/route.go is the only place the value is chosen, and it returns the same value for an allowed origin.
